notes: Form: {vocab_iid}--{term_code}. Immutable; do not reuse an identifier for a different concept.

description: Machine-readable code stored in registry/data fields when this vocabulary governs a value.
notes: Use lowercase kebab-case. Stable after publication; prefer deprecation to changing a code.

description: Preferred human-readable label for the concept.
Alternative labels, synonyms, abbreviations, spelling variants, or source-specific renderings.
notes: When multiple values are present, separate them with an unpadded pipe: value1|value2.

description: Definition of the concept represented by this term.
notes: Use the canonical external definition when adopting a published standard; otherwise write a project-local definition.

description: concept_iid of the immediate broader or parent concept in a hierarchical vocabulary.
notes: Leave blank when the vocabulary is not hierarchical or the concept has no broader term.

description: Lifecycle state of the vocabulary concept.
notes: Deprecated concepts remain in the vocabulary so historical data can still be interpreted.

description: Date the concept record was first added, in ISO 8601 calendar-date form YYYY-MM-DD.

Notes describing where, when, or how the concept should be applied.
concept_iid values for associated concepts that are related but are not broader/narrower or equivalence mappings.
notes: Use an unpadded pipe between multiple concept_iid values.

description: External concept identifiers or URIs judged to have the same meaning as this concept.
notes: Use an unpadded pipe between multiple identifiers.

description: External concept identifiers or URIs with closely related, but not identical, meaning.

description: concept_iid of the preferred successor concept when this concept is deprecated.
notes: Expected when status=deprecated and a direct successor exists.

description: Authoritative source for the concept or definition, such as a standard, citation, URL, or the lab-local registry standard.
notes: For adopted external vocabularies, prefer the canonical source rather than a secondary description.
